ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of every shareholder, director, UBO, authorized signatory, and commercial counterparty against Swiss SECO sanctions lists, Swiss FINMA/MROS publications, United Nations Security Council sanctions, EU consolidated sanctions, OFAC SDN/Consolidated Sanctions, and INTERPOL Red Notices. Additional enhanced due diligence is required for all PEPs and for high-risk jurisdictions under FINMA Circular 2016/7. For dangerous-goods freight licensure, screening must also verify that no consignor, consignee, or end-user is on Swiss export-control lists for dual-use goods and controlled hazardous chemicals.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Central Business Name Index (Zefix) and the Swiss Commercial Register, operated by the Federal Commercial Register Office under the Swiss Commercial Register Ordinance (SR 221.411), with filing via the official Tell/ID portal.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be in one of Switzerland's official languages (German, French, Italian, or Romansh) or use a clear Latin-script representation; names must not be misleading, contrary to public interest, or infringe prior third-party rights. The name of an Aktiengesellschaft must contain 'Aktiengesellschaft', 'AG', or the Latin 'SA' suffix. No transliteration into a non-Latin script is accepted for the registered name; foreign-language personal or geographical elements may be used only if clear and distinguishable on the Swiss register.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection by the Cantonal Commercial Register Office, the applicant may file a written administrative appeal with the competent Cantonal Commercial Register Supervisory Authority within 30 days of receipt of the rejection, stating the grounds and proposing an amended name. If the cantonal supervisory authority confirms the refusal, the applicant may lodge an administrative appeal with the Swiss Federal Administrative Court in St. Gallen or Bern, and ultimately appeal on grounds of public law to the Swiss Federal Supreme Court in Lausanne. The appeal must be lodged in written form, in an official Swiss language, with the challenged decision and evidentiary annexes.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office or correspondence-only address is not acceptable for an Aktiengesellschaft engaged in dangerous-goods forwarding. The registered office must be a physical address where the administration of the company is genuinely conducted, documents are kept, and directors can be reached during ordinary business hours. A serviced office or co-working suite may satisfy the requirement only if it provides actual workspace, reception, mail handling, file storage, and a contractual right to use the premises on a stable basis.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 45% within the first 24 months for the registered-offices and commercial-substance requirement. Unannounced physical inspection risk increases materially if the company holds a dangerous-goods freight forwarding licence, because the Swiss Federal Office of Civil Aviation (FOCA), the Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN), the Federal Spiez Laboratory, cantonal police, and the cantonal labor inspectorate all have statutory inspection powers under Swiss dangerous-goods transport, safety, and labour laws.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht, OR) Arts. 620-763 (Aktiengesellschaft), in conjunction with Art. 629 (paid-up capital), Art. 640 (registration), and the Swiss Federal Act on the Amendment of the Civil Code (Zivilgesetzbuch); implementing cantonal Commercial Register Ordinances (Handelsregisterverordnung, HRegV).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug), coordinated through the cantonal Notary and the Federal Commercial Register (FEDRO) for publication in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Articles of Association (Statuten) together with the Statutory Declaration of Incorporation (Gründungsbericht and Ausfertigung) authenticated by a Swiss public notary and filed for entry into the Commercial Register (Handelsregister).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum statutory share capital for an AG is CHF 100,000; at least 20% (minimum CHF 50,000) must be paid up at incorporation. Capital contributions must be deposited in a blocked escrow account (Sperrkonto) at a licensed Swiss bank, evidenced by a bank certificate; funds are released only upon successful Commercial Register registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION of [Company Name] AG, adopted at Zurich on [Date]. The Board of Directors hereby resolves by unanimous consent: 1. The subscriptions to share capital and the proof of payment through the blocked escrow account (Sperrkonto) are confirmed; the paid-up capital is placed at the free disposal of the Company. 2. The registered office is fixed at [registered street no.], [Postal Code] [City], Switzerland. 3. The following persons are appointed to the Board of Directors: [Name] as Chairperson and [Name] as Member; all signatories act with individual/collective signature. 4. The Board initiates all applications for commercial register entry and the Swiss dangerous-goods forwarding permits.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate name clearance and entity pre-approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Zug Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) via national Zefix portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a Zefix/Id search to confirm uniqueness of the proposed corporate name for an AG/SA; verify no conflict with existing registered legal entities or protected trademarks; reserve the name and obtain preliminary eligibility confirmation from the registry before drafting constitutional documents.
required_dossiers: Brief statement of corporate purpose aligned with ISIC 5229
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, submit a revised name variant with a justification letter, and re-file the pre-approval request within 10 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of Articles of Association and incorporation declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Notary Public (Notariat des Kantons Zug)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Appear before a Swiss notary to authenticate the Articles of Association (Statuten), the incorporation report (Gründungsbericht), and subscription declarations. The notary verifies the legality of the corporate purpose, the nominal share capital, number and nominee of shares, and the identity and capacity of all incorporators and founding directors.
required_dossiers: Identity and residency documents of incorporators and board members
Declaration of compliance with OR Arts. 622 and 629
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary issues a deficiency notice, amend the drafted clauses (e.g., share denominations or corporate object wording) and execute an addendum; re-notarization is required but no new registry fee applies.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Blocked escrow capital account and paid-up capital deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Swiss Bank (e.g., Zuger Kantonalbank, UBS, Credit Suisse) or PostFinance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a capital blocking account (Sperrkonto) in the corporate formation designation; deposit at least CHF 50,000 being 20% of the CHF 100,000 minimum nominal capital; obtain an official bank certificate confirming receipt. Full AML/KYC verification of signatories and all beneficial owners is mandatory before funds are credited.
required_dossiers: Bank account opening and AML/KYC forms
Capital deposit payment receipt and bank blocked-account certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank escalates its compliance review, supply legalized notarial translations and source-of-funds evidence; await the independent risk committee decision. Funds remain blocked until final Commercial Register certification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Register filing and statutory registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Zug Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary submits the complete incorporation dossier to the Commercial Register, including the authenticated Statuten, bank capital certificate, board mandate, and signature specimen forms, and requests immediate entry of the AG in the commercial register with an effective-date registration certificate (Handelsregisterauszug).
required_dossiers: Notarized board director signatures and powers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a query (Rechtsvorschlag), cure by supplementary declaration within 20 working days; any capital or article defect must be corrected through a notarial addendum. Failure to cure within 90 days invalidates the filing and requires re-initiation from Step 2.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Official Gazette publication and tax / UID / social insurance registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB), Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA), Cantonal Compensation Office (Ausgleichskasse)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon registration, the registry publishes the incorporation notice of the Zug Commercial Register. Thereafter, register for the VAT (MWST) under Art. 10 VAT Act, obtain the UID (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer) from ESTV, and register as an employer with the ISIC 5229 payroll classification for AVS/AHV, ALV, and BVG contributions.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a retroactive VAT or UID query is raised, file a corrective declaration with justification; if a late-registration penalty (Säumniszuschlag) is assessed, submit a written administrative grace petition with statutory grounds.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Dangerous goods forwarding license and DGSA appointment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Federal Office for Civil Aviation (FOCA/BAZL) Dangerous Goods Section and Federal Office of Transport (FOT/BAV), with facility inspection by Swiss Safety Center AG (SSC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the licensing dossier for ISIC 5229 specialized DG forwarding: appoint a certified Dangerous Goods Safety Advisor (DGSA/Gefahrgutbeauftragter) under ADR 1.8.3 and COMAT 1.8.3.2; file staff training records covering IATA DGR, IMDG and ADR; present the DG handling SOP, emergency response plan, and Swiss Safety Center facility inspection certificate; obtain the FOCA airfreight dangerous goods operator permit and, if road/rail multimodal services are to be performed, ancillary FOT/AVR permits.
required_dossiers: DGSA qualification certificate and appointment deed
Swiss Safety Center facility inspection certificate
DG handling SOP and emergency response plan
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the authority renders a deficiency notice, rectify within 60 days by revising the SOP, retraining staff, or amending the DGSA declaration; if the license is refused, appeal to the Federal Administrative Court within 30 days with full supporting remediations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Federal Office for Civil Aviation (FOCA/BAZL) and Federal Office of Transport (FOT/BAV) – Dangerous Goods Division, with technical facility inspections delegated to Swiss Safety Center AG (SSC)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Swiss Dangerous Goods Forwarding and Handling Operating Permit (Gefahrgut-Transportlizenz) under SDR/ADR and COMAT, ISIC 5229

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN/BAFU) – Division of Environmental Impact Assessment and Pollution Prevention
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B Registration / Sectoral Environmental Review: not a full EIA for DG transit or forwarding activities; full Environmental Impact Report (UVPV Annex criteria) is triggered only where the DG staging/warehouse area exceeds defined volumetric and hazardous-tonnage thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: comply with Waters Protection Ordinance (GSchV) parameter limits for organic solvents, PAH and emergency firewater containment; Air emissions: LRV (Luftreinhalte-Verordnung) VOC threshold of 150 ppm at loading and transshipment points; Waste: VVEA (Technical Ordinance on Waste) controls for UN-classified residues and consignee returns; soil protection per Altlastenverordnung.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification by the Cantonal Fire Prevention Service and Building Insurance (GVA) under VKF norms; structural load and stability inspection certificate in accordance with SIA 461 for DG staging areas; occupational safety and workplace health clearance issued by Suva (Swiss National Accident Insurance Fund), including mandatory medical surveillance and CMR-gas monitoring for DG-handling personnel.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenoessische Steuerverwaltung / Administration federale des contributions / Amministrazione federale delle contribuzioni), Schwarztorstrasse 50, 3003 Bern, Switzerland. Official portal: www.estv.admin.ch (VAT e-services, DEVA electronic filing). Central business register portal: www.zefix.ch. Swiss UID public register: www.uid.admin.ch. Cantonal tax administrations retain competence for cantonal and communal direct taxes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the Aktiengesellschaft (AG) by notarial deed, deposit minimum share capital of CHF 100,000 (at least 50% paid in), appoint the board of directors, and file for entry in the competent Cantonal Commercial Register. Step 2: The Commercial Register entry automatically allocates the Swiss business identifier (UID / Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer), which is the master tax identity number for all federal, cantonal and communal tax purposes. Step 3: Register for VAT with the Swiss Federal Tax Administration via Form 'Registration as a VAT taxable person' (eService) or via the UID portal once annual worldwide turnover from taxable supplies in Switzerland exceeds CHF 100,000, or voluntarily for lower turnover. Step 4: A foreign-incorporated enterprise with a Swiss permanent establishment or performing taxable supplies in Switzerland must obtain a Swiss UID through the UID registry, appoint a Swiss fiscal representative for VAT where no Swiss domicile exists, and register with the ESTV VAT division before the first taxable supply. No separate federal tax ID is issued for corporate income tax beyond the UID.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. The Swiss AG is a resident corporation with unlimited tax liability on worldwide profits (Art. 52 ff. Federal Direct Tax Act / DBG). Direct federal corporate income tax is levied at a flat rate of 8.5% on profit after tax (effective burden approximately 7.83% on pre-tax profit); cantonal and communal profit taxes apply at combined rates of approximately 11% to 21% depending on the canton of registered seat. Distributions are subject to Swiss withholding tax of 35%, reduced or refunded under applicable tax treaties. No pass-through or partnership treatment is available for an AG; the entity is a per se corporation and cannot be disregarded for Swiss tax purposes. Capital tax is imposed at cantonal level.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Switzerland does not provide a check-the-box or other entity-classification election under domestic tax law; an AG is mandatorily subject to entity-level taxation. Available statutory elections and administrative arrangements include: (i) VAT group election (Art. 12 VAT Act) allowing closely held affiliated companies to be treated as one VAT taxpayer with joint and several liability; (ii) participation-relief election for qualifying dividends and capital gains (Art. 70 and 71 DBG plus cantonal equivalents); (iii) Swiss principal-company ruling election allowing centralisation of international purchasing, sales and logistics functions under a reduced federal and cantonal profit allocation; (iv) patent-box / IP-relief election in participating cantons, subject to a binding tax ruling; (v) election to treat foreign permanent establishments as separate taxpayers or to apply a tax-exemption method, as available under cantonal practice. Hybrid mismatch rules under OECD BEPS Action 2 are implemented statutorily and are not elective.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Swiss Value Added Tax (Mehrwertsteuer / TVA / Imposta sul valore aggiunto), governed by the Federal Act of 12 June 2009 on Value Added Tax (VAT Act, SR 641.20), administered by the Swiss Federal Tax Administration. Switzerland applies a single federal VAT; there are no provincial VAT, GST or sales-and-use taxes.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 annual worldwide turnover from supplies taxable in Switzerland (Art. 10 para. 2 let. a VAT Act). Foreign-established companies without a Swiss place of business or domicile are subject to compulsory VAT registration from the first taxable supply in Switzerland (no monetary threshold). Voluntary VAT registration is permitted from the first franc of turnover where input VAT recovery is sought. Since 1 January 2018, entry in the Swiss Commercial Register no longer triggers automatic VAT liability; the CHF 100,000 threshold applies uniformly to all taxable persons.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: None. Switzerland has no real-time fiscal clearance system, no mandatory transaction-level API reporting, no electronic invoice validation and no digital stamping regime for VAT purposes. E-invoicing is standardised but voluntary, using the Swiss QR-bill standard, Swiss Payment Standards 2025 and Peppol BIS 3.0 with Swiss Business Rules. A federal B2G e-invoicing mandate for federal procurement is being introduced progressively starting 2026, but it does not require API-based fiscal clearance. VAT returns are filed quarterly or half-yearly via ESTV e-Service; accounting and substantiation records must be retained for 10 years.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Art. 23 para. 1 VAT Act, supplies of goods are zero-rated if the supplier proves that the goods were physically exported from the Swiss customs territory and delivered to a recipient abroad. Under Art. 23 para. 2 VAT Act, services directly attributable to the export or import of goods are zero-rated, including international transport, freight forwarding, customs clearance, temporary storage, handling and ancillary logistics services for dangerous goods. For a DG forwarding business, the zero rating applies if the freight forwarding service forms part of a single supply directly connected with the physical cross-border movement of the regulated hazardous goods; the Swiss domestic leg of an international export transport retains the 0% rate where the single-supply and direct-attribution tests are satisfied. The service must be rendered by a Swiss taxable person and the transport chain must be fully documented. Swiss VAT law imposes no statutory 180-day foreign-exchange repatriation deadline; the 180-day benchmark reflects standard export-financing documentation and bank / export-credit verification practice rather than a Swiss VAT statutory condition.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration - Swiss e-dec / e-dec web export declaration (A- or B-number) confirmed by the Federal Office for Customs and Border Security (FOCBS) evidencing the physical exit of dangerous goods from the Swiss customs territory, including transit documentation where applicable.

Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / CMR - international contract of carriage plus the freight forwarder's receipt (Spediteur-Uebernahmebescheinigung), the dangerous-goods transport documentation (IMO/IMDG container packing certificate, IATA shipper's declaration for dangerous goods, ADR consignment note, material safety data sheet) and the commercial invoice and packing list.

Inward Remittance Certificate - in Swiss practice, a bank credit advice or SWIFT MT103 statement evidencing receipt from the foreign principal in foreign currency; no formal statutory Inward Remittance Certificate exists under Swiss VAT law, but the payment record must be retained in the substantiation file for the 10-year retention period.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Swiss VAT operates on self-assessment and zero-rating claims are subject to systematic ESTV audit. Consequences of wrongful zero-rating: (i) the VAT shortfall is retroactively assessed at the applicable rate (8.1% standard, 3.8% accommodation, 2.6% reduced) together with default interest from the original due date; (ii) simple tax evasion (Art. 97 VAT Act) is punishable by a fine of up to three times the tax evaded; (iii) qualified tax evasion or fraudulent use of false documents (Art. 98 VAT Act) carries imprisonment of up to three years or a fine; (iv) violation of procedural and record-keeping duties is subject to fines of up to CHF 8,000; (v) in fraudulent export chains involving forged customs papers, disappearing exporters or phantom goods, the ESTV may impose joint liability, disallow input VAT recovery and initiate criminal proceedings, with publication of final convictions.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB) and the Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority (FINMA)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland maintains full convertibility of the Swiss franc (CHF) for both current and capital account transactions. There are no exchange controls, no prior authorisation requirements for cross-border payments, and no restrictions on profit repatriation or capital outflows. The CHF is a freely floating currency; however, transactions must comply with Swiss anti-money laundering (AMLA), sanctions, and reporting obligations under the Federal Act on the Prevention of Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing. No differentiated convertibility regime exists for current versus capital account items.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory export proceeds surrender or mandatory conversion ratios in Switzerland. Exporters are free to retain, use, or invest foreign currency proceeds without any obligation to repatriate or convert into CHF. This liberal regime is subject only to standard banking and tax transparency requirements, including proper bookkeeping and potential documentation requests under double taxation treaties or FATCA/CRS.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: Medium — Swiss-licensed fintech and electronic money institutions (EMIs) such as Swissquote and Bank Cler offer digitally facilitated corporate onboarding, but the dangerous-goods freight forwarding sector triggers enhanced due diligence. Offshore / non-Swiss digital EMIs are generally Low viability because Swiss banks and FINMA-regulated entities must apply equivalent rigorous AML/KYC standards; unregulated offshore EMIs cannot provide Swiss resident corporate accounts for letters of credit or high-risk trade settlement without a physical nexus and full regulatory oversight.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Swiss anti-money laundering law requires a face-to-face verification or an equivalent video-identification procedure approved by FINMA. For a high-risk corporate client engaged in dangerous goods (DG) forwarding, Swiss tier-1 banks typically mandate at least one physical interview with the ultimate beneficial owner and senior management. Fully remote onboarding is rarely accepted for this industry tier without an existing banking relationship or strong compliance sponsorship. The bank may also require the Swiss director to be personally present, especially when opening a Capital Escrow Account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Industry classification as high-risk (dangerous goods forwarding / ISIC 5229) triggering enhanced due diligence
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: valid hazardous materials transport licence (SDR / ADR / IATA DGR certifications), Swiss Federal Office for Civil Aviation (FOCA) or FOT approvals, standard operating procedures for DG handling, and compliance manual demonstrating internal controls.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex or opaque beneficial ownership structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: organisational chart, certified copies of shareholders registry, proof of identity for each UBO, and explanation of the business rationale of the holding structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained cross-border payment flows to/from high-risk jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: third-party audit / financial statements, detailed transaction ledger, underlying trade contracts and invoices, and evidence of economic substance in Switzerland.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Presence of sanctions-related trading partners or counterparties
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: real-time sanctions screening output, independently conducted sanctions risk assessment, written trade compliance policy, and terminable counterparty clauses in commercial contracts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Letter of credit (LC) / trade finance involvement in high-risk cargo
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: draft LC terms, proforma invoices and packing lists, certificates of origin, transport documents (B/L, AWB), and classification per UN dangerous goods regulations.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections into the Swiss AG must be wired via SWIFT MT103 or SEPA/CHF wire transfer to the Capital Escrow Account opened at the Swiss bank. The payment must include the beneficiary reference and a purpose code categorised as 'capital contribution / equity injection' (e.g., Swiss National Bank reporting code 'K8' or standard bank purpose code 'Capital Contribution'). For non-resident shareholders, the wire must be supported by a board resolution approving the capital increase, a Swiss notary deed, and evidence of the payment's origin to satisfy AML checks. The bank will verify the source of funds, and the payment must be in CHF or freely convertible foreign currency; no exchange control approval is required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for outbound trade settlements include: (a) SWIFT MT103 for direct wire transfers to foreign beneficiaries for operational expenses, freight settlements, and non-documentary payments; (b) Commercial Letters of Credit (documentary credits) presented through the bank's trade finance desk for goods involving hazardous materials, with SWIFT MT400/MT410/MT700 message types; and (c) International Bank Account Number (IBAN) transfers within the Single Euro Payments Area (SEPA) for EUR-denominated dispatches to EEA counterparties. The DG forwarding company must attach the necessary conformity certificates and transport documents to trigger payment under the LC.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX forwards (CHF/USD/EUR) with licensed Swiss banks under FINMA rules
Cross-currency swaps for longer-term trade receivable/payable matching
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in restricted or less liquid currencies subject to underlying genuine trade exposure
Plain vanilla FX options (puts/calls) for premium-based hedging of trade cash flows

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory financial statements (balance sheet, income statement, notes) and statutory audit report filed with the Commercial Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) of the registered office, coordinated via the Swiss Commercial Register platform and published in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 12 months after the balance sheet date per Art. 958e and Art. 699 OR; calendar-year AG: by 31 December of the following year; Annual General Meeting must approve the annual report within 6 months of fiscal year end (by 30 June for calendar-year companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default notice and administrative fine; enforcement and publication costs charged to the company; in persistent breach, the Commercial Register may commence ex officio strike-off and liquidation proceedings under Art. 935 OR

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial owners (Transparenzregister declaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Federal Office of Justice (Bundesamt für Justiz, FOJ) – Transparency Register (Transparenzregister) under the Swiss Money Laundering Act (Art. 71a et seq. GwG)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation of the registered beneficial owner dataset due on the Transparency Register's annual verification cycle; any change in beneficial ownership, including share transfers exceeding the 25% control threshold, must be reported within 30 days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fines under the GwG for intentional false or incomplete reporting; administrative fines for negligent noncompliance; personal director liability; noncompliant entities may be blocked from certain licensing and capital market transactions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Swiss VAT return (annual settlement) or quarterly VAT returns depending on the Federal Tax Administration assessment basis
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (FTA / ESTV, VAT Division)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual settlement taxpayers: within 60 days after the reporting year; quarterly filers: within 60 days after each calendar quarter; calendar-year companies: annual return typically due by 1 March of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge; default interest on unpaid VAT (currently 3.5% p.a.); tax fine up to three times the evaded tax for intentional violation; criminal prosecution for VAT fraud

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Ordinary audit (ordentliche Revision) is mandatory under Art. 727 OR if the AG exceeds any two of three thresholds for two consecutive fiscal years: balance sheet total over CHF 20 million; annual turnover over CHF 40 million; average of 250 full-time employees. Limited audit (eingeschränkte Revision) applies to AGs not exempt; audit dispensation is available only for AGs with fewer than 10 full-time employees if all shareholders consent and no listed securities or statutory exception apply. The dangerous-goods forwarding license (SDR/ADR) does not exempt the AG from audit obligations.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss GAAP under the Code of Obligations (Art. 957–963b OR); consolidated accounts may apply Swiss GAAP FER or IFRS; annual financial statements must be prepared by the board, examined by the statutory auditor, and submitted to the AGM within 6 months of fiscal year end; accounting records and vouchers must be retained for 10 years per Art. 958f OR.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The AG must maintain an internal beneficial ownership register and file beneficial owner data in the FOJ Transparency Register under the Swiss Money Laundering Act (GwG); a beneficial owner is any natural person holding more than 25% of capital or voting rights or otherwise controlling the AG; any change, including transfer of DG-forwarding business interests, must be reported within 30 days; the board of directors must confirm the registered data annually on the FOJ verification cycle and must update the statutory shareholder records in the Aktienbuch before each Annual General Meeting.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Shareholders (Aktienbuch) per Art. 686 OR – continuously updated for transfers of registered shares
Minute Book (board and general meeting minutes) per Art. 713 and Art. 731 OR
Beneficial Ownership Register (internal, reconciled with the FOJ Transparency Register)
Statutory accounting records and vouchers retained per Art. 958f OR (10-year retention)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $3,000 - $8,000 (limited audit typical for an SME AG; ordinary audit and consolidated audits are higher)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 8.5% Direct Federal Tax (effective 7.83% pre-tax equivalent); combined cantonal/municipal rates yield a statutory head-line range of 11.9%–21.0% depending on canton and commune, e.g. Geneva ~14.0%, Zurich ~21.0%, Zug ~11.9%
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory time-limited tax holidays in Switzerland. Available permanent measures include the participation relief (95% of qualifying dividend income exempt), the notional interest deduction on excess equity in some cantons, and cantonal 'license box' regimes for special-purpose IP income. A DG forwarding AG is typically not eligible for preferential IP boxes; ordinary combined rates apply.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual corporate tax return for stock companies: 'Steuererklärung juristische Personen' / 'Déclaration fiscale des personnes morales'. Filed electronically through the competent cantonal tax authority's e-filing system; Direct Federal Tax and cantonal/communal taxes are assessed in a single tax assessment procedure. After e-filing an approved tax return, the AG receives a combined assessment order (Veranlagungsverfügung / décision de taxation).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual. Fiscal year generally equals calendar year; non-calendar-year accounts require prior cantonal approval. Interim tax prepayments are generally invoiced quarterly based on the latest assessment.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The statutory filing deadline is 31 March of the year following the tax year for calendar-year taxpayers. Professional representatives may obtain an automatic/administrative extension to 30 June or 30 September; the cantonal tax authority may impose a written reminder before imposing penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box A. Company identity and UID (SHAB)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter exact legal name, domicile, Swiss Commercial Register number, UID (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer), date of incorporation, and authorized signatories.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign DG forwarding company with a Swiss branch or permanent establishment files as a taxable non-resident entity: input the UID of the Swiss branch, term of the registered PE/office, and full identity of the foreign head office.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declare worldwide gross turnover from freight forwarding, dangerous-goods logistics, transport, special warehousing, and ancillary charges (CON), net of discounts and Swiss freight tax elements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PE must include only gross Swiss-source revenue attributable to the Swiss PE plus cases of Swiss transfer-pricing attribution under the OECD profit-attribution rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declare deductible expenses: driver salaries, leased vehicles/vessels, aviation and multimodal charter costs, DG handling fees, insurance, rents, licence compliance, and communication overheads.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PE may deduct expenses directly attributable to the PE, including arm's-length payments to the foreign head office, limited to the extent economically linked to Swiss-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box D. Interest, royalties, and other financial income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declare bank interest, bond interest, dividends from subsidiaries, royalties, and exchange differences separately, because statutory exemptions and withholding-tax offsets are then applied.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident entities must disclose all Swiss-source interest and dividend income, claiming DTA reduction or refund of any anticipatory tax withheld, and attach Form 823 or refund form.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box E. Net taxable corporate income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: State the final corporate profit after loss carryforward, participation exemption, realized tax-allowed provisions, and all other adjustments. This is the basis for the 8.5% federal tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PE reports the Swiss PE net taxable profit after arm's-length TP adjustment; the federal and cantonal rate of the PE's Swiss jurisdiction is applied to the PE allocation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box F. Tax-at-source offset and prepayments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declare paid Swiss withholding tax (anticipatory tax) on Swiss dividends, bond interest, and lottery gains; offset against the tax due or claim refund under the applicable DTA.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the 35% Swiss anticipatory tax withheld on Swiss-source dividends/interest of a non-resident; attach the TRC and beneficial-owner form to obtain DTA relief or refund.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file within the time limit triggers a procedural fine (Ordnungsstrafe/amende) set per canton, generally CHF 100–5,000; after formal reminder, daily/set surcharges may be imposed. Assessment is then made on an estimated basis with loss of deduction claims; intentional tax evasion exposes the AG to a monetary penalty of up to 200% of evaded tax and criminal tax-fraud sanctions (fine plus imprisonment). Interest on late payment accrues at the statutory annual rate, currently 3.5% for direct federal tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Swiss anticipatory tax (Verrechnungssteuer/impôt anticipé) of 35% is withheld on dividend distributions and similar profit distributions by Swiss AGs; this statutory rate is reduced or refunded under DTA.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke treaty relief, the beneficial owner of the dividend must be tax-resident in the applicable DTA jurisdiction. For a withholding at source, present a valid DTA residence certificate (TRC) and a Form 823 / R-2 or current FTA relief form to the Swiss paying agent or bank before payment. Where full 35% has been withheld, the recipient must file a refund claim with the Swiss Federal Tax Administration within three years of the end of the calendar year of payment, together with the original dividend coupon, detailed ownership chain, TRC covering the period, and the Swiss Form 824 / claim for relief. Reduced treaty rates commonly applied are 0–5% for qualified substantial shareholdings and 10–15% for portfolio dividends depending on the treaty.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties paid by a Swiss AG to a non-resident have no Swiss withholding tax at source under domestic law. Interest on ordinary commercial loans, bank deposits, and intercompany current-account balances also are not subject to Swiss anticipatory tax. However, interest payable on taxable Swiss bonds and money-market securities is subject to 35% anticipatory tax, reduced to 0–10% under most Swiss DTAs. Treaty relief requires the same TRC plus Form 823 for interest on 'Kollektivanlagen', while royalties generally require no domestic withholding and only benefit from treaty-specific protection against income tax in source state.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Swiss tax law does not impose a fixed value-based Local File/Master File threshold for all entities. Mandatory country-by-country reporting applies to multinational groups with consolidated global revenue of CHF 900 million or more. For local transfer-pricing documentation, Swiss practice requires a Local File for companies with more than 250 employees, total assets above CHF 20 million, or turnover above CHF 50 million, or whenever intercompany cross-border transactions exceed CHF 5 million in a tax year; group-wide Master File is expected above the same group-size safe harbour (SME relief threshold).
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland applies an anti-abuse substance doctrine, distinct from EU-style ESR, under which an AG must have real personnel, premises, decision-making, administrative functions, and economic activity in Switzerland. Letterbox or pure domiciliary companies are taxed as fully taxable Swiss entities or substantially denied treaty benefits. For a DG forwarding company, required substance includes a Swiss business address, operational licences under the Swiss Dangerous Goods Ordinance (SDR 741.621), ADR/IMDG-certified personnel, genuine board and shareholder meetings in Switzerland, and actual management of hazardous-goods transport.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion / Tax fraud under Swiss direct tax law
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately suppressing shipping invoices, over-declaring intercompany expenses, creating fictitious DG storage charges, double-entry manipulation of freight income, or issuing false invoices for dangerous-goods consignments to shift profit offshore.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative surcharge up to 200% of evaded federal/cantonal tax plus 3.5% per annum interest; criminal tax fraud carries a public-law fine up to the tax evaded plus damages and imprisonment up to 5 years; prosecution within 10 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Members of the Board of Directors and officers are personally liable for deliberate false declarations; sanctions include attachment of private assets (civil restitution to the tax authority), travel bans where criminal proceedings have started, 10-year statute of limitations, and possible custodial sentence of 6 months to 5 years for tax fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company / sham substance and abusive treaty shopping
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the DG forwarding AG as a letterbox with no office, no hazardous-goods qualified staff, no board autonomy, and management performed from a shell in Zug or abroad; misrepresenting residency to claim DTA exemptions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of CIT assessment at preferential rates, disallowance of group tax relief, restitution of unfairly obtained treaty benefits, additional taxes of 25–35% plus interest, and licence revocation of the DG transport licence; civil penalties and prohibition to exercise a Swiss commercial activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign substanceless financial statements and tax returns are exposed to personal liability for restitution of lost Swiss taxes, directors' disqualification, seizure of Swiss bank and private assets, and imprisonment in aggravated cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer pricing mispricing and non-arm's-length cash flows
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intercompany DG forwarding invoices calculated at arbitrary margins, group-wide cost-allocation without benefits test, Swiss entity bearing all risk with insufficient capital, non-interest-bearing shareholder loans, or unjustified high-price international demurrage charges directed to tax-haven affiliates.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment of taxable profit by the Swiss tax authority; assessment of hidden profit distributions subject to 35% anticipatory tax; back-transfer of tax, penalty surcharge up to 100–200%, and 3.5% arrears interest; criminal fine and mandatory revision of annual accounts if adverse audit report.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Swiss director can be held civilly liable for corporate tax debts if he/she knowingly authorized abusive TP schemes; board members may be joined as defendants in tax withdrawal procedures, and travel measures (confiscation of passports) may be ordered during criminal tax proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML and sanctions violations in hazardous-goods cash flow / trade remittances
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting cash or crypto proceeds from non-bank counterparties for DG freight, deliberately ignoring beneficial-owner identification in high-risk corridors, facilitating transfer of dangerous goods to embargoed jurisdictions in breach of Swiss SECO sanctions and FATCA/AML obligations, or structuring Swift wire payments to avoid SAR thresholds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Anti-money-laundering supervision measures; administrative fines up to CHF 500,000 for serious violations in the financial intermediary sector; confiscation of profits, closure of Swiss banking relationships, reporting to the Money Laundering Reporting Office; parallel customs criminal proceedings and penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Prolonged disregard of AML and sanctions diligence exposes directors to Swiss AML criminal prosecution (including imprisonment), personal restitution, travel bans and denial of residency/immigration rights, and disqualification from serving as Swiss board members; the corporate veil is not a defence once criminal negligence is proven.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: False reporting under the Swiss Anticipatory Tax and Swiss VAT
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to withhold 35% anticipatory tax on actual dividend/concealed distributions; issuing fictitious VAT invoices on cross-border DG forwarding and claiming input VAT deductions without a Swiss VAT licence; invoicing without mandatory QR-bill reference data.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Withholding tax at 35% is shifted to the company; imposition of unpaid withholding tax plus 5% penalty and interest; VAT evasion fines of up to 300% of connected tax; loss of deduction of input VAT; publication of liability in Swiss Official Gazette.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Executive directors who knowingly omit withholding-tax declaration or VAT payments are personally liable for the company's tax debt and exposed to criminal fines/imprisonment up to 3 years; private assets may be arrested and a commercial prohibition issued.
